restoration_note: The teaching is a doctrine of five discrete degrees of divine emanation — Father of Greatness → Third Ambassador → Jesus the Radiance → Mind of Light → Form of Light — each producing a threefold power-set. The vast majority of gaps are short editorial completions of fixed Manichaean titles and formulae (ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲡⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ, ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ, ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ, ⲡⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ, ⲁⲩⲟⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ doublet) tightly constrained by visible traces; these I confirm. Strongly constrained also are {38}=ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ (King of Honor — fixed by lexicon and the reading's identification of the Lilou's Father). Left unrestorable: {32} (the prepositional phrase containing the bi-faced gaze, est. 6 chars but no controlled parallel), {39} (epithet of the Son, ~4 chars with no constraint), {40} (7-char speech-introduction with no formula visible), and {31} only partially constrained (feminine 'great X of light' — proposed ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ at low confidence given character count). Cross-line lacunae {27}/{28} below the Judge's tabernacle resolved low-confidence as 'under the place of the wheel of the stars.'

restorations.basis: Editor's fill; resumes the refrain 'one came forth from another' — ⲛⲧⲁ ⲟⲩⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ; ⲁⲛ = 'again' fits the iterative emanation pattern of the five Fathers.
ⲡⲉⲧⲉ relative pronoun before ⲙⲛ̄ ϣⲓ — standard Coptic relative.
ⲁⲧⲉϩⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ 'no measure to (his) Greatness' — completes the abstract from ⲙ̄ to ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ; lexicon: Greatness = ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ.
ⲙⲟⲛⲟⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'Only-Begotten' — visible ⲙⲙ + ⲛⲟⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ requires ⲟ.
ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ 'the first' continues across the line break; lexicon: first = ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ.
ϯⲟⲩ ⲛⲓⲱⲧ 'five Fathers' — the established formula stated explicitly in §390.
ⲁϩⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ — perfect of ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'to call/emanate'; required verbal ending.
ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲡⲉ 'the first is' — visible ⲣⲡ requires ϣⲁ.
ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲟ 'the Great (Spirit)' — the Mother of Life, called forth as first triad-member of the First Father; visible ⲡⲧⲛⲁ requires ⲟ.
ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲡⲉ 'the second is' — fixed ordinal formula in this teaching's enumeration.
ⲡⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the Beloved of the Lights' — lexicon-fixed title.
ⲉⲧⲟ ⲛⲉⲁⲩ ⲡⲉⲧⲧⲁⲓⲁⲓⲧ 'who is glorious, the honored one' — standard appositive sequence.
ⲡⲉⲧⲧⲁⲓⲁⲓⲧ ⲡⲉ — completion of qualitative + copula before next clause.
ⲁϩⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'has been revealed' — perfect of ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ; visible ⲱⲗⲡ requires ⲁϩⲟⲩ.
ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧϥ 'from him' — visible ⲁⲃⲁ + ⲏⲧϩ requires ⲗ ⲛ̄ⲍ.
ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ 'the Third Ambassador' — lexicon-fixed; the Second Father in the chain.
ⲛⲥⲩⲙⲃⲟⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all the counselors' — Greek loan complete + 'all'.
Standard 'who came forth from (the First Father)' formula matching §411 and §422; the Third Ambassador's pedigree clause before the recapitulation in §405 begins.
Article ⲡ at line start — with ⲉⲧⲉϣⲁⲩϯ creates the relative 'the one through whom they give eternal life,' Jesus the Radiance.
ⲧⲥⲟⲫⲓⲁ — Sophia, name of the Virgin of Light.
ⲛ̄ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ 'of the Archons' — visible ⲱⲛ requires ⲁⲣⲭ; the heart-stealing of archons by Sophia's image is the standard Manichaean episode.
ⲛϩⲏⲧ 'heart' — the pride-of-heart (ⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ) of the Greatness; visible ⲛϩ-ⲧ requires ⲏ.
ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'Mind of Light' — lexicon-fixed first faculty and first power of Jesus the Radiance.
ⲧⲁϩⲙⲉⲥ 'called' — completion across line break of ⲧⲁϩ-/-ⲉⲥ.
ⲡⲛⲁⲟ ⲛ̄ⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ 'the Great Judge' — standard Manichaean title; the Judge whose tabernacle is in the air, second power of Jesus the Radiance.
Genitive ⲛ̄ before ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ — 'souls of men.'
ⲉⲣⲉ ⲧⲉϥⲥⲕⲏⲛⲏ 'while his tabernacle' — circumstantial ⲉⲣⲉ + 3rd-masc. possessive; the Judge's tabernacle.
ϩⲁ ⲡⲙⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'under the place of the wheel of the stars' — standard locational expression for the Judge below the zodiac/sphere; ⲡⲙⲁ fits 3 chars. Conjectural.
Genitive ⲙ̄ⲡ before ⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ; editor's note 'likely article ⲡ' fits 'ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ' = 'of the wheel.'
ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'of the stars' — genitive of plural; lexicon: stars = ⲛⲥⲓⲟⲩ.
ⲡⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ — lexicon-fixed Coptic for Jesus the Radiance / the Youth; the third power's name continues across the page.
ⲧⲛⲁⲟ ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the great Maiden of Light' — feminine ⲧⲛⲁⲟ requires fem. noun; ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ is the standard pairing for Lilou-the-Youth in Manichaean texts. Char-count is approximate.
6 chars between ϩⲙ and ⲉⲓⲥⲉⲭⲉ ⲁⲧⲡⲏ ('gazing toward heaven'); could be ⲡⲉϥϩⲟ, ⲡⲣⲏ ⲡⲟⲟⲍ, ⲟⲩⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ, etc., none constrained by lexicon, parallels, or trace. Honest non-restoration.
ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ 'in the calling' — visible ⲙ̄ requires ϩ.
Conjunction ⲙ̄ⲛ̄ between ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ and ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ — 'the Calling and the Hearing,' lexicon-paired doublet for this two-faced power.
ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ idiom 'stand firm' — standard before ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ ϩⲁⲧⲙ ⲡϥⲓⲱⲧ.
ⲡϥⲓⲱⲧ 'his Father' — completion of the noun.
ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'the King' — definite article required.
ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'King of Honor' — lexicon-fixed (ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛ̄ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ); the reading explicitly identifies the bi-faced power as standing 'before his Father the King of Honor.' 5 chars fits.
~4 char epithet of ⲡⲥⲏⲣⲉ 'the Son' — could be ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory,' ⲡⲣⲏ 'sun,' or other; no parallel formula or trace constrains the choice. Honest non-restoration.
7-char speech-introduction after 'saying' (ⲉϥⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ); could be ϫⲉ + various openers (ϫⲉ ⲡⲉⲧⲉ, ϫⲉ ⲁⲗⲏⲑⲱⲥ, etc.) without controlling parallel. Honest non-restoration.
ⲁⲛⲁⲕ 'I am' — the saying 'I am the one who has seen him with my Father.'

restorations.proposed_english: this is what I say to
restorations.basis: Bridge from 'with my Father' to 'you also' (ϩⲱⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ); standard speech-formula completing the saying that mirrors John 8:38.
Parallel to §434's 'with my Father' (ϩⲁⲧⲙ̄ ⲡⲁⲓⲱⲧ); the saying 'what you have seen with your Father is what you do' mirrors the Johannine pattern, structurally fixed by the antecedent.
ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'come/go forth' — visible ⲃ requires ⲱⲕ; standard idiom for departing the body.
ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ 'three' — confirmed by §445-446 which counts off 'these are the three angels.'
ⲉϩⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ 'to hold/grasp' — confirmed by parallel ⲡⲉⲧⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲣⲏⲧⲉ in §444 (the third angel holds the diadem).
ⲁⲩⲟⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they were disclosed' — verbal pair with ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'were revealed,' standard Manichaean revelatory doublet (lexicon: reveal = ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ / ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ).
ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ '(of) them, their' — required for sense 'before their faces.'

Standard pairing 'the righteous, the faithful' (δίκαιοι καὶ πιστοί) in Manichaean designations of the elect; followed by 'men of peace and mercy' completes the standard quartet of qualifications for the elect receiving garments of light.
